corpus_row.citation: Murphy TM, Belmonte M, Shu S, Britt AB, Hatteroth J (2009) Requirement for abasic endonuclease gene homologues in Arabidopsis seed development. PLoS ONE 4(1):e4297. Claim supported: this is the record's own reference; it establishes genetically that the Arabidopsis abasic (AP) endonuclease genes, including ARP, are host DNA-repair genes required for normal seed development.
corpus_row.expected_class: not a TE - host AP (apurinic) endonuclease / redox factor ARP, a base-excision-repair gene
corpus_row.why_safe: Confusion axis: plant ARP is an APE1/ExoIII-family abasic endonuclease, i.e. the Exo_endo_phos/DNase-I-like fold shared with the LINE-1 ORF2p EN domain - the same trap as Rrp1, sampled from a second kingdom. Tool-independence: the cited paper's evidence is loss-of-function genetics (seed-development phenotype of insertion lines), not homology-based annotation. mRNA deposit, complete cds 9..1625, single locus, no LTR/TIR/TSD/RT/transposase content. Note: I deliberately did NOT cite Babiychuk et al. 1994 PNAS (the original Arabidopsis Arp AP-endonuclease enzymology) because I could not confirm that ACB29409.1 in this record is the same locus as Babiychuk's ARP - the two 'ARP' deposits encode proteins of different length (Z49776 CDS 49..1938 -> 629 aa vs this record's 538 aa) and Murphy et al. deposited multiple abasic-endonuclease homologues. The AP-endonuclease label is safe either way; only the choice of citation was affected.
